features.method: Derived: intersection of two circles on a local equirectangular plane (R = 6371008.8 m). Centres: centroids of OSM ways 331249625 (Chooz B1, 4.7890472 E 50.0895090 N) and 331249628 (Chooz-B2, 4.7912861 E 50.0898134 N), 163.3 m apart (published separations: 160 m NUCLEUS, 165 m Double Chooz 2021; 140 m in the 2006 TDR map caption). Radii: the far-detector baselines of the Double Chooz TDR, 1114.6 +/- 0.1 m and 997.9 +/- 0.1 m (Sec. 2.1, Table 3; rounded 1115 m and 998 m in arXiv:2009.05515). Assignment: the TDR labels the cores RE and RW, which does not map onto the OSM unit names unambiguously, so the shorter baseline is given to B2 because the Double Chooz PRD 86, 052008 Table V predicts more far-detector antineutrino events from B2 than from B1 (3422.4 vs 2910.9 with both reactors on; equal nominal power, flux ~ 1/L^2, so B2 is the nearer core; the distance ratio alone would give 1.25, the table gives 1.18). Mirror choice: the circles meet at two points mirrored about the B1-B2 line, [4.7983783, 50.0975486] and [4.8026591, 50.0845889]. Terrain from the IGN RGE ALTI service: the plant ground is 114.7 m and the Double Chooz TDR gives ~300 m.w.e. of 2.8 g/cm3 rock (~107 m) over the far hall; the northern solution is at 138 m a.s.l. (about 23 m above the plant, no such overburden possible) and the southern one at 239 m on a hill; the southern solution is also the one 209 m from the OSM 'Chooz A' building, as the TDR says the hall is 'close' to Chooz A. Sensitivity: the baseline of the two circle centres is only 163 m for ~1 km radii, so a 5 m error in the core separation moves the point ~25 m and a 20-30 m perpendicular offset of one core from its building centroid rotates the pair and moves it ~100-170 m; accuracy_m 200 is set accordingly.

features.method: OpenStreetMap way 331249709 (building=yes, 542 m2) kept verbatim. Identified as the building that hosts the VNS only by position: it is the only OSM building that contains the trilateration solution of the NUCLEUS baselines (see geometry:chooz-vns-position); no source names or outlines the building. The two checks compare its centroid distances to the B1/B2 centroids with the VNS-to-core baselines at 15 % tolerance, because the room is not centred in the building and the centroids are not core axes.

features.method: Derived: intersection of the circles of radius 72 m about the centroid of OSM way 331249625 (Chooz B1) and 102 m about the centroid of way 331249628 (Chooz-B2), the VNS-to-core baselines of the NUCLEUS paper (arXiv:1905.10258 Sec. 2.1: 72 m to B-1, 102 m to B-2), on a local equirectangular plane; the circles overlap in a thin lens 59 m wide, so the two mirror solutions are 59 m apart. The paper says the VNS room lies in the basement of a five-story office building between the two reactors; the southern solution lies inside OSM building way/331249709 (8.9 m from its centroid) whereas the northern solution is 67 m from that building and inside no building, so the southern one is adopted. The paper adds that the VNS 'is not centered with respect to the building'. The circles are drawn about building centroids, not core axes (the OSM unit footprints are ~15 000 m2), so accuracy_m 40 covers a 20 m offset of each core.

summary.plain: The Chooz nuclear power plant's reactor buildings (the old Chooz A unit and the two Chooz B units), the computed positions of the Double Chooz far laboratory in the hill and of the NUCLEUS very-near-site room between the two Chooz B units. The Double Chooz near laboratory is not located.

unlocated.backlog: A Double Chooz near-detector civil-engineering plan or paper figure with a scale, the EDF CNPE de Chooz site plan that the NUCLEUS paper credits for its Fig. 2 (which marks the near and far sites), or an OSM/IGN feature for the near-lab shaft building. The four candidate points are listed in docs/atlas-worklog/RELEASE_GEOMETRY_underground.md.
unlocated.reason: The near laboratory (~400 m from the cores; 469 m and 355 m to the two cores per arXiv:2009.05515, 120 m.w.e.) has two mirror solutions for each of the two ways the two distances could be paired with B1/B2, and none of the four is selected by a fetched source: the terrain test that settles the far laboratory does not separate them (IGN ground elevations at the four candidates are 114.8 and 105.7 m on the west side of the plant and 132.2 and 107.9 m on the east side, against a plant ground level of 114.7 m, so none sits under a clear hill), and the near-site design figures differ between the TDR (a ~40-45 m deep shaft, 'an overburden of 30 meters of rock') and later papers (about 120 m.w.e., ~400 m from the cores).
